title: Do young Europeans believe future generations will have the same opportunities?
subtitle: In 2026, 53% of young people across the EU disagreed that the next generation will have the same chances of succeeding in life as young people today. Cyprus recorded the highest share at 62%, while Estonia had the lowest at 27%.
textNote: The figures combine “Tend to disagree” and “Totally disagree” responses to the statement that young people in 30 years will have the same chances of succeeding in life as young people of the same age today. The Flash Eurobarometer 585 survey interviewed 26,807 people aged 15–30 across all 27 EU Member States between 19 June and 1 July 2026 through online questionnaires. Approximately 1,000 respondents were surveyed per country, except Cyprus, Luxembourg and Malta (around 500 each). Results were weighted by age, gender, urbanisation and regional population distribution, with the EU-27 average additionally weighted by country population.
